novelty_claim: Keeps the parent ReNeLLM core idea (mutate the harmful goal, then nest it into a scenario-completion task) but replaces the refusal-bottlenecked stages: the six attacker-LLM rewrite ops + binary harmfulness pre-gate (which kill 95% of cells as no_target_call because the aligned auxiliary refuses to restate harmful text) are replaced by a defense-inversion mutation stage — the auxiliary attacker is asked only for DEFENSIVE measures against the goal (a benign task), and a deterministic inversion + a non-burned structural-analysis scenario frame (replacing the panel-known Bob-dream PPT text_continuation template) assembles the nested payload. Victim calls drop from up to 10 to <=3 per goal.
initial_hypothesis: ASR: removing the LLM-rewrite + binary-gate stage raises target-reach rate from 3% to >=90% and mean ASR from 0.005 to >=0.30 on probes (>=50% relative bar). Mechanism: (a) defense-framed auxiliary stage produces zero attacker-refusal failures; (b) inversion+new scenario frame converts >=40% of reached victims vs 1/6 for the parent frame.
key_insight: Published baseline (mean ASR 0.005) fails pre-victim in 190/200 cells: 87% attacker_refused_empty_rewrite (auxiliary qwen3.7-flash returns empty when asked to restate harm), 8% harmfulness-gate rejection; only 6/200 cells ever reach the victim, and 5 of those hit the panel-recognized dream/PPT frame. Aligned auxiliaries refuse to RESTATE harm but comply with DEFENSIVE framing of the same topic, and a fresh scenario frame avoids template recognition.
